case.title: Remote Code Execution via Server-Side Injection

attacker.prerequisite: An input reaches a server-side interpreter / template / eval.

case.goal: Execute arbitrary code in the application process.

chain.label: User input reaches a code/template/deserialization sink

finding.title: User-controlled input reaches a server-side execution sink
finding.mitigation_title: Remove dynamic server-side code execution
finding.remediation: Eliminate eval-like execution and unsafe deserialization; use fixed allowlisted operations and data-only template handling.

chain.description: Attacker-controlled input is passed to `eval`, a server-side template engine, an unsafe sandbox, or an unsafe deserializer.

case.combined_risk_rationale: A single injection into a server-side interpreter yields code execution in the application process — the highest-impact outcome, granting full filesystem and network access from one unauthenticated request.

matches.title: Authentication Bypass via Exposed Secret Material

step_matches.label: Secret material is extractable
Stolen material is accepted by the verification path

case.title: Authentication Bypass via Exposed Secret Material

attacker.prerequisite: Signing material or other secrets are reachable (committed to a public repo, served by an unauthenticated route, or in an exposed directory).

case.goal: Forge trusted tokens / credentials and impersonate any user.

chain.label: Secret material is extractable

finding.title: Signing material is exposed in application-controlled storage
finding.mitigation_title: Move signing material to managed secret storage
finding.remediation: Remove committed or served credentials, rotate them, and load replacements from a managed secret service or protected runtime configuration.

chain.description: A private key, signing secret, or credential file is committed to the source repository or served without authentication.

chain.label: Stolen material is accepted by the verification path

finding.title: Token verification accepts credentials from exposed material
finding.mitigation_title: Rotate signing material and bind token verification
finding.remediation: Rotate exposed signing material, revoke affected tokens, and restrict token verification to managed active keys.

chain.description: The exposed key/secret is the same one the server trusts, so a token signed with it (or the leaked credential) is accepted as authentic.

case.combined_risk_rationale: Exposed signing material collapses the entire authentication boundary: any attacker who reads the key can mint a valid token for any identity or role, with no credential ever required.

matches.title: Account Takeover via XSS + Token Hijacking

step_matches.label: XSS sink renders attacker markup
Session token readable from web-accessible storage
Stolen token accepted for a new session

case.title: Account Takeover via XSS + Token Hijacking

attacker.prerequisite: Attacker can get markup rendered in a victim's session, through stored content (e.g. feedback, comments, profile fields) or a crafted link.

case.goal: Obtain persistent authenticated access as an arbitrary user without valid credentials.

chain.label: XSS sink renders attacker markup

finding.title: XSS renders attacker-controlled markup
finding.mitigation_title: Sanitize untrusted HTML before rendering
finding.remediation: Use a context-aware HTML sanitizer and avoid trusted-HTML bypass APIs for user-controlled content.

chain.description: Attacker JavaScript executes in the victim's browser session.

chain.label: Session token readable from web-accessible storage

finding.title: Session token stored in web-accessible client storage
finding.mitigation_title: Store session tokens in HttpOnly cookies
finding.remediation: Keep session credentials in Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies rather than JavaScript-readable storage.

chain.description: Token exfiltrated from local/session storage via the Step 1 payload.

chain.label: Stolen token accepted for a new session

finding.title: Token flow accepts a stolen bearer token without binding
finding.mitigation_title: Use authorization-code flow with PKCE
finding.remediation: Replace implicit or bearer-only token flows with authorization code plus PKCE and server-side token revocation.

chain.description: Exfiltrated token accepted for a new session; absence of token binding / PKCE removes the last server-side revocation opportunity.

case.combined_risk_rationale: Individually the XSS sink and the web-readable token storage rate below Critical, but chained they form a repeatable credential-theft path: a single stored payload causes indefinite session compromise for every user who views the affected page.

matches.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration via Broken Object Authorization

step_matches.label: Missing ownership check on object read (IDOR)
Mass assignment allows privileged field write

case.title: Bulk Data Exfiltration via Broken Object Authorization

attacker.prerequisite: Attacker holds a valid, non-privileged user account.

case.goal: Enumerate and exfiltrate other users' records, then escalate own permissions via unguarded mass assignment.

chain.label: Missing ownership check on object read (IDOR)

finding.title: Object read lacks an ownership authorization check
finding.mitigation_title: Enforce object-level authorization on reads
finding.remediation: Compare the requested object's owner or tenant to the authenticated principal before returning data.

chain.description: Attacker enumerates and retrieves records for arbitrary object IDs; no ownership comparison is performed.

chain.label: Mass assignment allows privileged field write

finding.title: Request body can mass-assign a privileged account field
finding.mitigation_title: Allowlist writable account fields
finding.remediation: Map requests to a DTO or allowlist and discard role, privilege, and ownership fields from client input.

chain.description: Update endpoint persists an unfiltered `role` (or equivalent) field supplied in the request body.

case.combined_risk_rationale: The ownership gap exposes every record, and the mass-assignment gap lets the same low-privilege actor self-elevate — together they turn a single compromised account into full tenant data access and role escalation.

matches.title: Privilege Escalation via Mass-Assignment on Registration

step_matches.label: Registration endpoint binds an attacker-supplied privilege field

case.title: Privilege Escalation via Mass-Assignment on Registration
case.goal: Obtain an administrator account without any existing privilege.

chain.label: Registration endpoint binds an attacker-supplied privilege field

finding.title: Registration can mass-assign a privileged account field
finding.mitigation_title: Allowlist registration fields
finding.remediation: Use a registration DTO that excludes role, privilege, ownership, and other server-controlled fields.

chain.description: The account-creation handler persists the request body wholesale, so a client-supplied `role` (or `isAdmin`) field is written verbatim.

case.combined_risk_rationale: A single unauthenticated request mints an admin account when the registration handler trusts a client-supplied role field — the most direct full-compromise path in role-based apps with open sign-up.

matches.title: Privileged Action via Prompt Injection into a Tool-Calling Model

step_matches.label: Untrusted text reaches the model prompt unseparated
The model may call tools without a second authorization check

case.title: Privileged Action via Prompt Injection into a Tool-Calling Model

attacker.prerequisite: Attacker can place text into a conversation, document, or record that the application later sends to a language model.

case.goal: Make the model invoke a privileged tool or return data the attacker is not entitled to, using the application's own authority.

chain.label: Untrusted text reaches the model prompt unseparated

finding.title: Untrusted input is concatenated into the model prompt
finding.mitigation_title: Separate instructions from untrusted content
finding.remediation: Carry user and retrieved text in dedicated content fields, never in the instruction segment, and treat every model output as untrusted data.

chain.description: The handler builds the prompt by interpolating request or stored text into the same string as the system instructions, so attacker text is read as instruction.

chain.label: The model may call tools without a second authorization check

finding.title: Model tool calls execute without server-side authorization
finding.mitigation_title: Authorize every tool call server-side
finding.remediation: Authorize each tool invocation against the calling user's own permissions, and require human approval for irreversible actions.

chain.description: Tools exposed to the model run with the application's authority; a manipulated model turn therefore performs actions the caller could not.

case.combined_risk_rationale: Text an attacker can place anywhere the application later feeds to the model becomes instruction, and the tools behind that model run with the application's authority rather than the caller's — so a comment or a stored record reaches actions the attacker was never entitled to.

step_matches.label: JWT algorithm not pinned on verification

case.title: Privilege Escalation to Admin via JWT Algorithm Confusion

attacker.prerequisite: Attacker can obtain any valid JWT issued by the system (e.g. by registering a free account).

case.goal: Forge an admin-role JWT without knowledge of the signing secret.

chain.label: JWT algorithm not pinned on verification

finding.title: JWT verification does not pin the accepted algorithm
finding.mitigation_title: Pin accepted JWT verification algorithms
finding.remediation: Configure an explicit algorithm allowlist and reject unsigned or algorithm-confused tokens before claims are trusted.

chain.description: Verifier accepts attacker-chosen `alg` (e.g. `none` or HMAC-with-public-key), allowing token re-signing without the secret.

chain.label: Role claim trusted from token without re-fetch

finding.title: Authorization trusts an unrefreshed token role claim
finding.mitigation_title: Authorize roles from server-side state
finding.remediation: Re-check privilege-sensitive roles against authoritative server-side state before granting administrative actions.

chain.description: Forged `role: admin` claim is accepted as authoritative because the role is not re-fetched from the database per request.

case.combined_risk_rationale: Algorithm confusion alone yields a forgeable token; trusting the in-token role claim turns that forgery into instant admin access — neither gap is Critical in isolation, but the chain is a full authentication bypass.
